# openalexAPI

> **Alpha.** openalexAPI works and is tested, but its functions,
> arguments and the details of its responses may still change between
> versions. It is not on the openalexPro r-universe yet; install it from
> GitHub.

**openalexAPI** serves a local Parquet corpus of OpenAlex works through
a web API that answers like the [OpenAlex
API](https://api.openalex.org). You can run the same queries against
your own data that you run against OpenAlex: classic `filter=` /
`search=` URLs, OQL (OpenAlex Query Language), OQO (OpenAlex Query
Object), `group_by`, `sort` and paging. It also includes a small web
page for running queries in the browser.

Because the answers look like OpenAlex’s, the download functions of
[openalexPro](https://github.com/openalexPro/openalexPro) work against
the local server unchanged. Point
[`pro_query()`](https://openalexpro.github.io/openalexPro/reference/pro_query.html)
at it with `endpoint =`.

The corpus can come from:

- [`openalexPro::pro_request_parquet()`](https://openalexpro.github.io/openalexPro/reference/pro_request_parquet.html)
  /
  [`pro_fetch()`](https://openalexpro.github.io/openalexPro/reference/pro_fetch.html)
  downloads
- an extraction from the OpenAlex snapshot (openalexSnapshot)
- any other source with the OpenAlex works schema

It is meant for **project-sized corpora**, not the whole snapshot.

## Installation

openalexAPI is not on the openalexPro r-universe yet. Install it from
GitHub; its dependencies, openalexPro included, come along:

``` r

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("openalexPro/openalexAPI")       # main: the current alpha version
pak::pak("openalexPro/openalexAPI@dev")   # dev: the newest changes
```

Or with remotes:

``` r

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("openalexPro/openalexAPI")
```

## Quick start

``` r

library(openalexAPI)

# A corpus downloaded with openalexPro, or any folder of works Parquet files
serve_corpus("my_project/parquet", port = 8000)
```

Then open <http://127.0.0.1:8000/> for the web page, or query the API:

``` R
http://127.0.0.1:8000/works?filter=type:article,publication_year:>2015&search=coral bleaching
http://127.0.0.1:8000/works?filter=type:article&group_by=authorships.countries
http://127.0.0.1:8000/?oql=works where type is article and year >= 2015
http://127.0.0.1:8000/works/W2741809807
```

From another R session, download a subset of the corpus with
openalexPro, exactly as from OpenAlex:

``` r

library(openalexPro)
q <- pro_query(
  entity = "works", type = "article", search = "coral bleaching",
  endpoint = "http://127.0.0.1:8000"
)
pro_fetch(q, project_folder = "subset")
```

## How it works

``` R
classic URL or OQL --> OpenAlex /query (free) --> OQO --> DuckDB SQL --> OpenAlex-shaped JSON
OQO                -----------------------------^  (offline)
```

[`prepare_corpus()`](https://openalexpro.github.io/openalexAPI/reference/prepare_corpus.md)
(run by
[`serve_corpus()`](https://openalexpro.github.io/openalexAPI/reference/serve_corpus.md))
reads the Parquet files into a cached DuckDB database. The cache holds
one row per work, IDs and DOIs normalised so they match in any form, and
full-text indexes over title and abstract. OpenAlex’s free `/query`
endpoint translates classic URLs and OQL into an OQO, so the query
languages are exactly OpenAlex’s.
[`oqo_to_sql()`](https://openalexpro.github.io/openalexAPI/reference/oqo_to_sql.md)
compiles the OQO into SQL. An OQO sent directly runs without network
access.

## What is supported

- **48 works filters:** type, year and dates (also the creation date),
  language, open access, citations and percentiles, authors and ORCIDs,
  institutions (also with their lineage), countries, funders, sources,
  ISSNs, publishers, topics down to subfields, keywords, SDGs, IDs
  (OpenAlex, DOI, PMID, PMCID), `cites` and `cited_by`. AND, OR (`a|b`),
  negation (`!a`), ranges, and `null` for “field missing” all work.
- **`group_by`** on one dimension, with OpenAlex’s key formats.
  `:include_unknown` is supported.
- **Full-text search** over title and abstract, with `search`,
  `search.exact` and the `<field>.search` filters, plus searches in
  affiliation strings and author names. All words must match, quoted
  phrases must appear in order, proximity (`"a"~N~"b"`, `"a b"~N`)
  works, and wildcards work with `.exact`. Results are ranked by
  `relevance_score` (BM25).
- **Records** are returned as stored, including fields that are not
  OpenAlex’s. You can use `select`, `sort`, `per_page`, `page`, `cursor`
  and `sample`/`seed`, and look up single works by ID or DOI.

## Differences from OpenAlex

- **Local data:** counts come from the corpus, not from all of OpenAlex.
- **Search** covers title and abstract only, because there is no full
  text. The stemmer folds more word forms than OpenAlex’s, so stemmed
  counts can be higher. Proximity allows up to N words between the
  terms, an approximation of OpenAlex’s.
- **Display names:** countries, languages and licenses use the code as
  the display name in `group_by` results (“AU” rather than “Australia”).
- **Unsupported features** get a clear HTTP 400 that names them:
  OpenAlex collections, semantic search, `group_by` on several
  dimensions, and OQL’s comparisons and nested queries. 156 of
  OpenAlex’s 174 OQL example queries run locally
  (`tools/oql_coverage.R`).

## Corpus size and memory

![Query times, database size, build time and memory for 10,000 to 9.6
million works](reference/figures/scaling.svg)

Query times, database size, build time and memory for 10,000 to 9.6
million works

These figures come from `tools/benchmark.R` (75 queries covering every
feature) on parts of the OpenAlex snapshot, run on a Mac with 14 cores
and 36 GB of RAM (`tools/benchmark_scaling.csv`, figure by
`tools/plot_scaling.R`):

| Works       | Parquet | Database | Build  | Median query | Slowest query | Queries \> 1 s |
|-------------|---------|----------|--------|--------------|---------------|----------------|
| 10,000      | 0.02 GB | 0.04 GB  | 2 s    | 0.01 s       | 1.8 s         | 1 of 75        |
| 100,000     | 0.18 GB | 0.5 GB   | 14 s   | 0.04 s       | 2.5 s         | 3 of 75        |
| 1 million   | 1.6 GB  | 7 GB     | 1 min  | 0.05 s       | 4.9 s         | 3 of 75        |
| 4.9 million | 8.6 GB  | 28 GB    | 5 min  | 0.29 s       | 18 s          | 16 of 75       |
| 9.6 million | 21 GB   | 63 GB    | 13 min | 0.74 s       | 51 s          | 33 of 75       |

- **The database** (the cache built by
  [`prepare_corpus()`](https://openalexpro.github.io/openalexAPI/reference/prepare_corpus.md))
  takes 3 to 7 times the space of the Parquet files: about 7 GB per
  million works.
- **Queries stay fast while the database fits in memory.** Up to a
  million works the median query takes 0.05 s whatever the size. Once
  the database is larger than the RAM (here above about 5 million
  works), DuckDB reads from disk and queries get much slower. The
  slowest are long searches, `group_by` on references or keywords, and
  200 records per page with all fields.
- **Building** needs more memory than serving: about 14 GB at a million
  works. Larger corpora use all the RAM and write to temporary files on
  disk, which works but slows the build down.

Recommendations:

| Works | RAM | Disk for the cache | Use |
|----|----|----|----|
| up to 1 million | 16 GB | up to 10 GB | interactive, on a laptop |
| up to 5 million | 32 GB or more | up to 40 GB | interactive; heavy queries take seconds |
| about 10 million | 64–96 GB (estimate) | 70 GB | needs a server; on 36 GB, occasional queries only |

Put the cache (`cache_dir`) on a fast local SSD. The whole OpenAlex
snapshot (over 250 million works) is out of scope.

## Running on a server

[`serve_corpus()`](https://openalexpro.github.io/openalexAPI/reference/serve_corpus.md)
serves the API and the page from one process, so it can run on a server
for a group. Each release is published as a Docker image,
`ghcr.io/openalexpro/openalexapi`. With `docker/compose.yaml` and
`docker/Caddyfile`, a server needs only Docker and the Parquet files:
[Caddy](https://caddyserver.com) in front adds HTTPS with a free
certificate. The vignette’s section “Running on a server” has the steps,
plus what the server does not do (logins, more than one request at a
time).

See
[`vignette("openalexAPI")`](https://openalexpro.github.io/openalexAPI/articles/openalexAPI.md)
for the details.

# Package index

## Serving a corpus

Prepare a Parquet corpus and serve it as an OpenAlex-compatible API.

- [`serve_corpus()`](https://openalexpro.github.io/openalexAPI/reference/serve_corpus.md)
  : Serve a corpus as an OpenAlex-compatible API
- [`prepare_corpus()`](https://openalexpro.github.io/openalexAPI/reference/prepare_corpus.md)
  : Prepare a Parquet corpus for serving

## Query compiler

- [`oqo_to_sql()`](https://openalexpro.github.io/openalexAPI/reference/oqo_to_sql.md)
  : Compile an OQO into DuckDB SQL

## Package

- [`openalexAPI`](https://openalexpro.github.io/openalexAPI/reference/openalexAPI-package.md)
  [`openalexAPI-package`](https://openalexpro.github.io/openalexAPI/reference/openalexAPI-package.md)
  : openalexAPI: Local OpenAlex-Compatible Web API over a Parquet Corpus
